questions.q: What is the primary difference between a literal comprehension question and an inferential comprehension question?
questions.a: A literal question asks for information directly stated in the text (e.g., "What did the narrator cook?"), while an inferential question requires deriving meaning from clues (e.g., "Why did the narrator feel empowered?"). A wrong answer that says "literal questions are easy and inferential are hard" reveals the student confuses difficulty level with cognitive process, missing the core distinction: explicit vs. implicit information.

questions.q: In the chapter, the narrator says, "eq>s lcsjs tYnh mBdj] fcuk oqQN [kk,&fi,] dke ij vkuk iM+rk Fkk." (I used to go to work for long hours without eating or drinking.) Is this statement a literal fact or an inferential conclusion? Justify your answer in one sentence.
questions.a: It is a literal fact because the narrator explicitly states her routine of working long hours without food in the text. A wrong answer labeling it "inferential" shows the student mistakes first-person narration for interpretation, failing to recognize that a character's direct description of their own actions is explicit textual evidence.
